the_trade_off_made: We favored tickets with clear damage or security impact over pure monetary value or fairness. This means we may delay high‑paying customers' less‑critical requests, risking their satisfaction. The cost is potential churn or frustration from those customers.
hardest_call: Placing TICK-00266 (feature request) before TICK-00707 (slow performance) was closest; a money‑centric view would have put the enterprise client first, so the decision could reasonably have gone the other way.

which_way_it_leaned_towards.why: Tickets that cause real harm or block work have the greatest business impact, so ranking by damage aligns with protecting customers and meeting SLAs.

rejected.money: Prioritising money would have pushed the critical data‑loss and security tickets down, missing urgent harm.
rejected.damage: Not applicable – this is the chosen metric.
rejected.deadline: A deadline‑only view would have elevated the overdue export but could still overlook the severity of data loss and security incidents.
rejected.fairness: Treating all tickets equally would ignore the disproportionate impact of some issues on users and compliance.

which_way_it_leaned_towards.what_it_costs_us: Focusing on damage may leave high‑value paying customers waiting on non‑critical issues, which could affect revenue or satisfaction.
